title: The chairman's secret
summary: Six in the morning, and the chairman is asleep in his car in the club car park with his coat over him. His house is sold. He's been paying the wages out of his own pocket for a year, and he makes you promise not to tell. A season on there's a buyer, and he needs you in the room.

ends.title: The fans' club
ends.text: The fans' trust bought the club for a pound and its debts. The chairman has a season ticket now, row K, and brings his own flask.

ends.title: Sold on
ends.text: The club was sold to a man with a helicopter. The chairman sends you a Christmas card from his sister's spare room.

ends.title: The secret out
ends.text: Everyone knows now what the chairman did. The town gave him a dinner. He hated every minute of it.

p-not-a-word.text: Not a word to anyone about {chairman.short} and the car

kept.text: Nobody hears it from you. He nods at you in the corridor, every time now.

broken.text: "I asked you for one thing." His office door stays shut.

beats.title: Six in the morning

event.title: Six in the morning
event.speaker: chairman
setup: You're in early for the gym. The chairman's old estate is in the corner of the car park with the windows steamed up, and he's asleep in the passenger seat with his coat over him and his shoes on the dashboard.
You knock. He wakes up like a man who's been caught.

say: "Don't," he says. "Get in, it's warm." A carrier bag with a shirt in it. A box of bank letters. "House went in March. The wages have been mine since last summer. Don't look at me like that."
"Because if the town knew, the town would panic, and the players would go, and it'd be over by Christmas. I'll find somebody. Promise me. Not a word."

replies.label: "I'm telling the captain. He needs to know."
"The paper could find you a buyer."

promise.text: He shakes your hand and puts his shoes on. At nine he's in his office in a tie, like nothing happened.

captain.text: The captain goes very quiet and says the lads will want to know. By Friday they all do, and they train like it's a cup final.

paper.text: {reporter.name} runs it on the Thursday: CHAIRMAN SLEEPING IN CAR TO PAY WAGES. Three people ring the club wanting to help, and one wanting to buy.

beats.hint: The chairman is asleep in his car at the training ground

beats.title: The canteen

event.title: The canteen
event.speaker: chairman
setup: {canteen.short} puts your beans down and doesn't let go of the plate. "I've worked here twenty-two years and I know when something's wrong. My wages went in from a different account this month. Is the club all right?"

say: She lowers her voice. "I've a mortgage, love."

replies.label: "Somebody's looking after it. That's all I can say."

lie.text: She nods and lets go of the plate. She doesn't believe you, and she's kind about it.

half.text: "Somebody," she says, and looks towards the chairman's window. "Right." Extra beans the next week.

truth.text: She sits down on the stool behind the counter. Then she gets up and makes the chairman a bacon sandwich and takes it up herself. By lunch he knows who told her. "I asked you for one thing." His office door stays shut.
She sits down on the stool behind the counter. Then she gets up and makes the chairman a bacon sandwich and takes it up herself.

beats.hint: The canteen woman asks if the club's in trouble

beats.title: The buyer

event.title: The buyer
event.speaker: chairman
setup: A season on. Two offers. A man who owns car washes in four counties and wants to move the club to a ground by the motorway. And the fans' trust, who have a pound, a bucket of pledges and a plan to keep it where it is.
{if arc.path=='paper'}The chairman still hasn't forgiven you for the paper. He's asked you anyway.{/if}The chairman wants one player in the room. "They'll listen to you. They don't listen to me."

say: The car wash man has brought a model of the new ground with tiny trees on it. The trust has brought biscuits.

replies.label: "The club stays where it is. Sell to the fans."
"The car wash man has the money. Take it."
"It's not my place. I'm a player."

trust.text: The vote is four to three. The chairman signs the club over for a pound and gives the trust the pound back.

money.text: He takes the money. The model with the tiny trees goes in the trophy cabinet. The trust's biscuits stay in the boardroom for a month.

out.text: You sit at the back and say nothing. The car wash man wins on the chairman's vote.

beats.hint: A season on, there's a buyer, and the chairman wants you there

beats.title: Row K

event.title: Row K
event.speaker: chairman
setup: Two seasons on. The old chairman is in row K with a flask and a programme, in a coat that used to be his good one.
{if arc.mid=='truth'}{canteen.short} brings him a tea at half time and stands with him for the second half.{/if}

say: He waves you over at the final whistle. "The town wants to give me a dinner. Somebody's told them." He looks at you, then at the reporter in the press box.

replies.label: "Go to the dinner. Let them say thank you."
"Then tell them no. It's still yours to keep."

dinner.text: Three hundred people at the social club. He gets up to speak, says "well", and sits down again. They clap for five minutes.
He goes to the dinner and they make a fuss. Afterwards he says the trust's biscuits were better.
He goes to the dinner. He sends you the menu with a note on the back: THANK YOU FOR NOTHING. HA.

keep.text: He tells them no. Nobody ever finds out, and he likes it that way.
He says no to the dinner and goes to stay with his sister. A card every Christmas.
He says no, but everybody knows already.
